name: Fairmont Le Chateau Montebello
positioning: Fairmont Le Château Montebello, a log-built resort on the Ottawa River, midway between Montreal and Ottawa
best_for: Travelers who want a log-built resort with a spa, an aquatic center and a golf course

facts.text: The resort dates from 1930 and sits on the Ottawa River.
The resort was inspired by the châteaux of the Swiss Alps.
The resort is midway between Montreal and Ottawa.
Rooms mix rich woodwork with custom fabrics and rustic accessories, and have windows that open to let in fresh air.
The Deluxe Jacuzzi Suite has a two-person jacuzzi.
The restaurant Aux Chantignoles uses regional ingredients.
The aquatic center offers swimming and lounging, and there is a health club with indoor tennis and squash.
The hotel has a Fairmont Spa offering a variety of spa treatments.
Charging stations are available for Teslas and other electric vehicles.
The resort offers more than 40 activities and experiences on-site.

highlights.text: The resort was built with 10,000 giant red cedar logs, all cut and set by hand.
A six-sided fireplace with a central chimney is the focal point of the three-story atrium.
Fairmont River View rooms are located mostly on the first and second floors and have large windows offering views of the Ottawa River.
The golf course was designed by Stanley Thompson.

considerations.text: The hotel has a Resort Experience Fee, which includes outdoor self-parking for guests.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires travel planning for dining and entertainment options.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont Le Château Montebello
